121.01 Division Delay (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

If the eligibility decision is delayed beyond the 30th calendar day after the application date and the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) caused the delay in the first 30 days, send a written Notice of Decision (NOD) to the individual informing them that:

• the application is pending;

• what action(s), if any, they must take to complete the process;

• they must report all changes which have occurred since the application was filed; and

• the application will be denied if they fail to take the required action within 60 days of the date the application was filed.

If DHHS delays the eligibility decision beyond the 60th day after the application date and the eligibility information is otherwise complete, continue processing the application.

If the individual is eventually determined eligible, provide benefits retroactive to the original date of application.

If the individual is eventually found ineligible, deny the application. The individual is not entitled to retroactive benefits.

A delay is caused by DHHS if the worker fails to do any of the following:

• schedule a second interview appointment if the individual failed to appear for the first appointment but requested a second appointment within the 30-day period;

• inform the individual of work registration requirements and allow at least 10 calendar days from the date of notification for compliance;

• offer help in obtaining verification and allow at least 10 calendar days for the individual to provide missing verification; or

• offer help in completing DFA Form 800, Application for Assistance .

References : He-W 750.01, RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.2(h)(1)(i), (h)(3) & (h)(4)

121.03 Applicant Delay (FSM)

SR 00-19 Dated 06/00 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Deny the application by the 30th day if the individual fails to complete the application process. The individual is not entitled to benefits for the month of application. No advance notice period is required.

If the individual fails or refuses to provide required verification within 10 calendar days of the Department of Health and Human Services’s (DHHS’) request, and the worker has helped the individual when required, deny the application on the tenth day.

• If the individual complies after the denial, but before the 30th day, reactivate the application and provide benefits back to the original Filing Date of the Request for Assistance.

• If the individual complies between the 30th and 60th day, determine eligibility based on information in the original application and changes reported by the individual. They are not entitled to benefits for the month of application. Prorate benefits from the date they comply and enter a new Filing Date on the application.

Exception: Expedited service cases that are closed due to failure to provide verification within 30 days from the date of application must reapply for benefits. They cannot use the original application even if they provide verification between the 30th and 60th day.

• If the individual does not comply by the 60th day, deny the application and require them to file a new application. The individual is not entitled to any lost benefits, even if the delay in the initial 30 days was caused by DHHS.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.2(f), (g)(3), & (h)(2)

125.01 Eligibility Criteria for Expedited Service (FSM)

SR 97-13 Dated 05/97 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Applicants are entitled to expedited service if they meet one of the following criteria:

• The household has both of the following:

- countable liquid resources totaling $100 or less, and

- countable gross monthly income totaling less than $150.

• The household ’ s countable liquid resources and countable gross monthly income total less than their most recent monthly expenses for rent or mortgage and utilities. Allow the telephone standard for households with a telephone expense. Allow the full amount of shelter and utility expenses, even when some expenses may have been paid by a third party such as local welfare, fuel assistance programs, or charities.

*

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.2(i)(1), 7 USC 2020(e)(9)

body:
125.03 Destitute Migrant or Seasonal Farm Workers (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Migrant or seasonal farm workers are destitute if they have $100 or less of countable liquid resources and meet any of the following criteria:

• Their only income received for the application month is from a terminated source, and they will not receive any more payments from that source after the application date.

All their income in the application month is from a new source, and $25 or less is all they will receive from the first of the month up to and including the tenth calendar day after the application date (or the end of the month if there are less than 10 days left in the month).

• They have a combination of terminated income through the application date and new income after the application date if both of the following apply:

- there is no other income from the terminated source that month; and

- they will receive no more than $25 from the new source through the tenth day after the application date (or the end of the month if there are less than 10 days left in the month).

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.2(i)(1)(ii), 7 CFR 273.10(e)(3), 7 USC 2020(e)(9)

125.05 Frequency of Expedited Service (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

There is no limit to the number of times a household may be certified under expedited service procedures. Prior to each subsequent expedited certification, the household must do one of the following:

• provide verification that was postponed at the last expedited certification, or

• be certified under normal 30-day processing requirements since the last expedited certification.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.2(i)(4)(iv)

125.09 Time Frames for Expedited Service (FSM)

SR 11-09 Dated 01/11 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

*Generate a Notice of Decision (NOD) to the individual as soon as an eligibility determination is made, but no later than the seventh calendar day after the application date.

Eligible individuals must receive their Food Stamp benefits as soon as possible, but no later than 7 calendar days after the application date.

Exceptions:

• If the interview is done by telephone and the application must be mailed to the individual for signature, do not count the mailing time and the time the application is in the individual ’ s possession in the time frames.

• If the individual was entitled to expedited service on the date of application but the situation was not discovered until later, expedited service time frames begin on the date the situation is discovered.

• If the individual applied at an SSA office as a pure SSI household, expedited service time frames for delivery of Food Stamp benefits begin the day the correct District Office receives the application. Determine eligibility and allotment amounts, however, based on the date the individual filed the application at the SSA office.

• If the individual meets the expedited service criteria but cannot provide proof of identity and the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) worker cannot prove identity through documentation or collateral contacts, the expedited service time frames do not begin until the date the postponed proof of identity is provided.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.2(i)(3), (i)(4)(i), & (k)(1)(i)(F) & (J), 7 USC 2020(e)(9)

body:
125.13 Postponed Verification (FSM)

SR 23-18 Dated 4/23 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Applicants entitled to expedited service must verify identity before receiving their initial benefits unless an Authorized Representative (AR) applies for the individual.

When an AR applies, take the following steps:

1. Require verification of the AR’s identity; and

2. If necessary to meet timeframes for expedited service, postpone verification of the applicant’s identity.

Obtain verification of all other eligibility factors if possible, through collateral contacts or readily available documentation. However, do not delay delivery of benefits past the expedited time frames for eligibility factors other than identity. If necessary, postpone other verification.

Exception :

If the applicant is a blind or disabled resident of a group living arrangement, you must determine that the group living arrangement is an eligible facility before you issue expedited benefits.

Applicants who postpone verification and other program requirements must provide the required documentary evidence and comply with program requirements before receiving continued benefits.

New HEIGHTS will generate the AE0026, Verification Checklist , to notify the individual of all of the following:

• what information is needed;

• when the information is needed;

• that assistance may not be provided or may end if verification is not provided; and

• that if the expedited household’s benefit level changes as a result of the verification they provide, the changes will take effect without advance notice.

The New HEIGHTS-generated AE0026 is automatically generated anytime something is entered onto the Application Entry screen, marked "Not Yet Verified," and eligibility is run. If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, use the paper backup BFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance .

If the individual provides the needed evidence and complies with program requirements within 30 days of the application date, update the case within the earlier of the following time frames:

• 30 days from the application date; or

• 5 working days after receipt of the required verification, if the major run deadline for the second month’s benefits has passed.

Require a new application for expedited service cases that are closed due to failure to provide verification within 30 days of the date of application.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.2(f)(1)(vii) & (i)(4)(i); 7 USC 2020(e)(9)

127.01 Interview Sites (FSM)

SR 24-31 Dated 12/24 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

An in-person interview is conducted at the applicant’s local district office. The place where the interview is conducted must preserve the privacy and confidentiality of the interview.

Applicants are also able to choose to have a phone interview instead of coming into the District Office for an in-person interview. All phone interviews must preserve the privacy and confidentiality of the interview.

All program and verification requirements remain the same whether the applicant participates in a phone or in-person interview.

127.03 Failure to Appear for an Interview (FSM)

SR 11-09 Dated 01/11 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

If the individual fails to appear for an interview deny the application according to the following chart.

If by the 30th day after the file date... Then... the applicant has not requested another appointment… …deny the application. the applicant has requested another appointment… • …use DFA Form 807 or New HEIGHTS-generated CS0001 to reschedule the appointment, and • …hold the application open even if the appointment is after the 30th day. If the applicant... Then... misses the appointment… …deny the application on the 30th day or the day of the appointment, if the appointment was scheduled after the 30th day. keeps the appointment, and the appointment is on or before the 20th day after the application date… • …follow pending information policy (see PART 129 ), and • …ensure benefits are *issued by the 28th day after the application date. keeps the appointment, and the appointment is after the 20th day… • …allow the individual 10 days to provide needed information • …if information is received by the tenth day following the appointment, do the following: - if the individual is not eligible, deny the application by the 30th day after the application date (or on the same day information is received if after the 30th day). - if the individual is eligible, ensure benefits are *issued by the 28th day after the application date (if not possible, complete a manual issuance on the day the individual provides the needed information). • …if the information is not received by the tenth day, deny the application the following work day.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.2(e)(3)

body:
127 INTERVIEWS (FSM)

SR 24-31 Dated 12/24 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

At initial application and at least every 12 months for recertification, the household must participate in an in-person or phone interview.

Interviews are official and confidential discussions regarding an individual’s household circumstances. During the interview, the following will occur:

• An evaluation of all available information, including any existing case record;

• Resolution of any unclear or incomplete information;

• An individual’s rights and responsibilities are provided and reviewed; and

• Individuals are provided information about program policies and procedures.

An interview will be conducted prior to each initial certification and each recertification of eligibility.

If applicable, interview an authorized representative if the individual cannot participate in the interview because of age, incapacity, illness, transportation difficulties, employment, language barriers, or similar reasons.

Exceptions:

• Cases eligible for recertification via the mail-in or online recertification process are not required to participate in an interview, however, one must be granted if it is requested. DHHS may also require an interview as a result of reported changes or the discovery of conflicting information regarding eligibility criteria.(See PART 161 , RECERTIFICATION and Section 161.01 , Timely Notice); or

• An interview is not required at recertification for households who have no earned income and all adult members are elderly or disabled, provided the household meets all other recertification requirements.

References : He-W 722.01; RSA 161:4-a,IV; RSA 167:8; 7 CFR 273.2(d)-(e); FNS waiver 00005762

133.07 Public Assistance Households (FSM)

SR 25-22 Dated 07/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

To the extent possible, assign six month SNAP certification periods to coincide with public (cash) assistance redeterminations. If necessary to avoid delays in issuing benefits for the first month of the new certification period, assign a SNAP certification period that expires in the month following the public assistance redetermination month.

If public assistance is denied or terminated, shorten the certification period when household circumstances warrant. Notify the household of the new end date of the certification period.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.2(j)(1)(i), 7 CFR 273.10(f), 7 USC 2012(f)

body:
133 LENGTH OF ELIGIBILITY (FSM)

SR 26-23 Dated 08/26 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

SNAP eligibility is determined for a specific period of time, called the certification period. At the end of the certification period, entitlement to SNAP benefits ends.

When the certification period ends, the individual must reapply, be interviewed if required, and be determined eligible to receive SNAP benefits again.

SNAP households are certified for six months. At initial application, the month of application is the first month of the certification period even if eligibility is determined in a subsequent month.

Exceptions:

· Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Households are certified for 36 months. See section 133.01 ESAP Households .

· Extended Food Stamp (EFS) households are certified for five months from the month their financial benefits close. See Section 249.07 Extended Food Stamp (EFS) Period

· Households with unstable circumstances may be certified for less than six months.

· For recertification, the certification period begins with the month following the last month of the previous certification period.

References: He-W 746.02; RSA 161:4-a, IV; 7 CFR 273.10(f); 7 USC 2012(f); FNS waiver 00011190

body:
141.01 Administrative Appeal Requests and the ANP (FSM)

SR 13-19 Dated 09/13 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

If an individual requests an *administrative appeal within * 15 days from the date on the notice of the action being appealed , continue assistance at the pre-change level pending the *administrative appeal decision, and/or until the Food Stamp certification period ends. If an individual requests an *administrative appeal after the *15-days expire or if there is no ANP, the termination or decrease takes effect on schedule. The individual may choose to continue receiving benefits at the pre-change level pending the outcome of an *administrative appeal.

If the individual establishes good cause for failing to request an *administrative appeal within the *15 days, reinstate benefits at the pre-change level pending the *administrative appeal decision, and/or until the Food Stamp certification period ends.

When benefits are reduced or terminated due to a mass change, reinstate benefits at the pre-change level only if the appeal is requested within 15 days from the date on the notice of the action being appealed and the issue being contested is that eligibility or benefits were improperly computed, or that a federal law or regulation was misapplied or misinterpreted.

When benefits are continued or reinstated pending an *administrative appeal decision, reduce or terminate those benefits only if one of the following circumstances occurs:

• The certification period expires. The individual may reapply and be determined eligible for a new certification period, with a new benefit amount, pending the *appeals officer ’ s decision on the contested action.

• A change which affects the individual ’ s eligibility or benefit amount occurs while the *administrative appeal decision is pending, and the individual does not request an *administrative appeal during the new *15-day period.

• A mass change which affects the individual ’ s eligibility or benefit amount occurs while the *administrative appeal decision is pending.

• The *appeals officer makes a preliminary written determination at the *administrative appeal that the sole issue is of federal law or regulation and that the individual ’ s claim is valid.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.12(e)(6)(iii), 7 CFR 273.13(a)(1), 7 CFR 273.15(k)

141.03 No ANP Required (FSM)

SR 98-03 Dated 05/98 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

There is no Advance Notice Period (ANP) when any of the following circumstances result in termination of assistance, decreases in the level of eligibility, or decreases in the amount of benefits:

• The individual provides a written, signed request to terminate assistance.

• Individuals provide information in writing which they realize will result in the termination of assistance or decrease in the level of eligibility or amount of assistance.

• The individual ’ s location is unknown, and Department mail is returned by the Postal Service indicating no forwarding address is on file.

• For expedited service, there is no ANP for either of the following situations:

- the individual does not provide postponed verification within the 30-day time frame; or

- the individual provides verification within the 30-day time frame which results in termination or a decrease in benefits. Notify the individual at the time of certification that Food Stamp benefits will be adjusted without advance notice when the verification is received.

• The individual applied for a public assistance or SSI grant and Food Stamps at the same time and is receiving Food Stamps at the time the grant application is approved. Notify the individual at the time of certification that Food Stamp benefits will be adjusted without advance notice when the grant is approved.

• The state or federal government initiates mass changes.

• All members of the household have moved out-of-state.

• All members of the household have died.

• The individual has been getting a higher benefit amount to restore lost benefits, and the restoration is complete. Notify the individual in writing before the higher benefit amount ends.

• A household member is disqualified because of an intentional program violation (IPV), or the benefit of the remaining household members is terminated or reduced because of the disqualification.

• The individual ’ s benefit amount varies from month to month because of changes which were anticipated at the time of certification. Notify the individual at the time of certification that the benefit amount will vary.

• A household member subject to a strike or lockout begins receiving income due to employment or strike benefits, and the individual signed a waiver of the right to an ANP at the time of certification.

• A drug or alcohol treatment center or a group living facility loses its state certification or is disqualified as a retailer.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.13(C)

141 ADVANCE NOTICE PERIOD (ANP) (FSM)

SR 03-27 Dated 10/03 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Notify individuals in advance of termination of assistance, a decrease in the level of eligibility, or a decrease in the benefit amount. The time frame between the date the Notice of Decision (NOD) is generated and the date the action actually takes effect is called the advance notice period (ANP).

Exception: An advance notice period applies when positive and negative changes occur at the same time and result in a negative action .

The standard ANP is 10 calendar days. Under some circumstances the ANP is not required * or is increased to 30 days.

Terminations and decreases are effective for the first major run after the ANP expires.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.13(a)(1)

145.01 Reporting Requirements (FSM)

SR 25-23 Dated 06/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

All SNAP households, regardless of certification period, are ONLY required to report:

• lottery or gambling winnings, won in a single game before taxes or other withholdings, equal to or greater than $4,500

• changes that result in an ABAWD’s work hours falling below the requirement of 80 hours per month;

• changes that cause gross household income to exceed 130% of the current federal poverty income guideline for the household size

Exception: Consider households whose income exceeds the 130% threshold at the time of certification, to have met the special 130% income reporting requirements, and do not need to report any increase in income until their next recertification.

These changes must be reported by the 10th day of the month after the month in which the change occurred.

Households that have been certified for 36 months and no longer meet the ESAP criteria will be placed on an ESAP hold. Individuals in ESAP hold are considered regular SNAP households but must maintain their 36-month certification period. While on ESAP hold, they are required to report any changes in their household circumstances that may affect their benefits and eligibility to the department every six months on their periodic report.

Households receiving SNAP in addition to receiving financial assistance, medical assistance, or NH Child Care Scholarship must comply with the reporting and verification requirements of those programs. Workers must act on all reported changes for all programs, including SNAP

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.11(r); 7 CFR 273.12(a)(2); 7 CFR 273.12 (a)(5)(iii)(C)&(G); 7 CFR 273.12 (a)(5)(v);

145.03 What to Report (FSM)

SR 25-23 Dated 06/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

SNAP households must report the following changes during their certification period:

· Lottery or gambling winnings, won in a single game before taxes or other withholdings, equal to or greater than $4,500

· Changes that result in an ABAWD’s work hours falling below the requirement of 80 hours per month;

· Changes that cause gross household income to exceed 130% of the current federal poverty income guideline for the household size

Exception: Consider households whose income exceeds the 130% threshold at the time of certification, or who report a change in income over 130% during the certification period, to have met the special 130% income reporting requirements. These households are not required to report any further increase in income during the certification period.

· Households that are required to fill out a periodic report (see section 145.04 , Periodic Reports ) must report all changes that affect eligibility or benefit levels when their periodic report is due (every six months during their 36-month certification period).

SNAP households are not required to report changes in any other case circumstances during the certification period.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV ; 7 CFR 273.11(r); 7 CFR 273.12(a)(5)(iii)(C)&(G); 7 CFR 273.12(a)(5)(v);

145.04 Periodic Reports (FSM)

SR 26-05 Dated 02/26 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Periodic reporting is required for households that no longer meet the ESAP Criteria. Households that no longer meet the ESAP criteria must maintain their 36-month certification period and will be required to complete a periodic report every six months.

These households will be sent BFA form 478, Periodic Report , in the first week of the 5th month from the date they reported the change in their circumstances (and each six months thereafter until their recertification). On this form, the household must report the following changes:

Changes in Unearned Income:

· source; and

· amount of gross monthly unearned household income from a private source if the amount changes by more than $125 per month.

Changes in Earned Income:

· source; and

· hourly wage rate or salary if the change causes gross monthly earned income to change by more than $125 per month.

Other Changes That Must be Reported:

· household composition;

· residence and any resulting changes in shelter costs;

· the amount of legally obligated child support; and

· when an ABAWD’s work hours fall to less than 80 hours per month.

Households that are not categorically eligible (regular or expanded) for SNAP must also report changes in resources that put their household over the resource limit, including vehicles.

Changes reported are processed like any other change that has been reported in a SNAP case during the certification period. See PART 147 , ACTIONS ON CHANGES , PART 151 , CHANGES THAT INCREASE BENEFITS , and PART 153 , CHANGES THAT DECREASE BENEFITS .

All available databases (NECSES, BENDEX, VCI, SDX, Equifax) must be used to verify reported changes before verification is requested. Income or deductions that were not reported on the periodic report form do not need verification unless questionable.

The household must return the completed form by the 5th day of the following month. If the Periodic Report is filed by this date, benefits must be issued by the 5th of the following month.

If the household has not returned their Periodic Report by the due date, a reminder notice will be sent advising the household that it has 10 days from the date of the notice to file a complete report. If an eligible household files a complete periodic report during this 10-day period, and the case closed, the case must be reopened no later than the 15th of the following month. If the household does not respond to the reminder notice, the household's SNAP case will be closed, and the household will be sent a notice of decision.

If an eligible household that has been closed for failure to file a complete report files a complete report after the notice of decision was sent, but before the end of the following month, benefits will be reinstated at the appropriate level without proration.

If the household does not return their periodic report by the end of the month after it was due, the household must reapply.

If the household files a complete report resulting in reduction or termination of benefits, a notice of decision must be received by the household no later than the 5th of the following month. If the household fails to provide requested information or verification regarding a deductible expense, the household's benefits will be determined without regard to the deduction.

References : 7 CFR 273.12(a)(5)(iii); FNS Waiver 00011190

145.07 When to Report (FSM)

SR 25-23 Dated 06/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

At all eligibility interviews, applicants must report changes that have occurred since the application was filed and any anticipated changes expected to occur before the next recertification.

After eligibility is determined, the household must report required changes no later than 10 days from the end of the calendar month in which the change occurred, provided that the change occurred with at least 10 days remaining in the month. If there are not 10 days remaining in the month, the household must report within 10 days from the date the change occurred.

For changes to income and lottery winnings, consider the date that the change occurred to be the date the payment was received.

References : He-W 751.01; He-W 752.01(a); RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.12(a)(2)-(3)

SR 20-05 Dated 01/20 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

The State must seek to clarify and verify unclear information received outside the certification period when the Department receives unclear information from the Prisoner Match Report.

Federal regulations require that the State establish a matching system to ensure that SNAP benefits are not issued to individuals who are incarcerated for more than 30 days. Incarceration includes local, state, and federal facilities. Information on incarcerated individuals is received from the Social Security Administration. This information is not considered verified upon receipt.

body:
161.01 Timely Notice (FSM)

SR 25-22 Dated 07/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Each household will be notified that they need to recertify their eligibility before their current certification period ends to determine eligibility for a new period and for benefits to continue.

Households shall be notified that they are required to participate in a regularly scheduled recertification via mail-in, face-to-face/phone or online based on their household circumstances.

Face-to-Face/Phone Recertification

A recertification interview letter is sent to household s who are required to participate in a face-to-face/phone recertification and is generated by the 15 th of the month prior to the month the recertification is due .

The letter advises the household of the following:

• the date and time of the eligibility interview;

• the household must call to reschedule the interview if unable to attend the appointment and wish to continue receiving benefits; and

• the date that the certification period ends.

The letter includes :

• BFA Form 775, Rental Verification Request ; and

• BFA Form 756, Employment Verification Request .

For a face-to-face/phone recertification the household must complete BFA Form 800R, Application for Continued Eligibility for Financial, Medical, Child Care, and SNAP Benefits , or indicate any changes on the Eligibility Interview Summary (EIS) and sign BFA Form 811S, Statements of Understanding ; and participate in a face-to-face/phone interview.

Online or Mail-In Recertification

Financial and/or medical assistance cases with related SNAP that meet criteria in the Adult Assistance Manual PART 155 , REDETERMINATION or the Family Assistance Manual PART 161 , REDETERMINATION , may participate in an online or mail-in recertification process.

Mail-In Recertification

A mail-in recertification package is sent to cases that are eligible for this type of recertification by the 15th of the month prior to the month the recertification is due.

The package includes:

• A Mail-In Recertification Letter ;

• BFA Form 800R, Application for Continued Eligibility for Financial, Medical, Child Care, and SNAP Benefits ;

• BFA Form 811R, Application: Your Rights and Responsibilities ; and

• a postage paid business reply envelope.

The letter advises:

• of verifications needed to process the case;

• of the date that the household's benefits will terminate if the household provides BFA Form 800R and needed verifications after the 15th of the following month; and

• to contact the District Office if they have any questions.

ESAP Mail-In Recertification

A ESAP mail-in recertification package is sent to ESAP households by the 15th of the month prior to the month the recertification is due.

The package includes:

• A Mail-In Recertification Letter ;

• A pre-populated HEIGHTS generated SNAP recertification form;

• BFA Form 811R, Application: Your Rights and Responsibilities ; and

• a postage paid business reply envelope.

The letter advises:

• of verifications needed to process the case;

• of the date that the household's benefits will terminate if the household provides their redetermination form and needed verifications after the 15th of the following month; and

• to contact the District Office if they have any questions.

Online Recertification

Recipients with NH EASY accounts who are scheduled for what would usually be considered a mail-in recertification are eligible to complete their recertification online.

If the NH EASY account holder’s recertification method is "online," the online recertification letter is generated by the 15th of the month prior to the month the recertification is due.

The letter advises:

• that the household must complete the online Recertification Application and send in all needed verifications by the 15th day of the following month;

• of the date that the household's benefits will terminate if the household does not complete the online recertification process and/or provide all needed verifications by the due date;

• that the household may opt out of the online recertification process and return to a mail-in recertification process; and

• that the household should contact the District Office if they have any questions.

The letter will also include:

• a postage-paid business reply Central Scanning Unit (CSU) envelope for the recipient to provide their verifications.

Households eligible to participate in the online or mail-in recertification process are not required to participate in a face-to-face/phone interview. However, an interview must be granted if one is requested by the household or by the authorized representative.

When verification is not sufficient or not provided in the online or mail-in redetermination process, send New HEIGHTS-generated AE0055, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance . If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, use paper backup BFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance .

References : He-W 766.01-.02; RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.2; 7 CFR 273.14

161.03 Required Verification for Recertification (FSM)

SR 25-22 Dated 07/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

The household must be notified in writing of any required information or verification needed to complete the recertification, and the due date for returning the information or verification.

New HEIGHTS will generate a verification checklist that includes the information/verification that is needed and the due date by which it must be provided.

If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, a paper backup BFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance shall be used

Deductions (including medical deductions) incurred by the household DO NOT need to be re-verified when:

• there have been no changes in the deductions; and

• the deductions have been previously verified by a third party.

Households do not need to re-verify previously reported ongoing medical expenses that exceeded $35 at their last certification.

The department shall assist households in obtaining missing verification when:

• the household is unable to provide verification due to circumstances beyond their control; or

• a request for information was sent or given to a third party and that party fails or refuses to cooperate.

If the attempt to assist the household is unsuccessful:

• the case record must document that the attempt was made, and that the household and the department were unable to obtain verification; and

• the household shall be allowed to self-attest in writing to verify the missing information.

The household must provide verification of all of the following:

• changes in income, including termination of employment, if the source changed, or if the amount changed by more than $50 per month;

• new medical expenses that exceed the standard medical deduction ($135), or changes in total recurring medical expenses of more than $35 per month;

• work hours, if ABAWD and not exempt from ABAWD work requirements; and

• other information which has changed. Unchanged information shall not be verified unless the information is incomplete, inaccurate, inconsistent or outdated.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; He-W 766.01; He-W 766.02; 7 CFR 273.2(f)(8); 7 CFR 273.14(b)(4)

161.05 Processing Recertifications (FSM)

SR 25-22 Dated 07/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

To receive a full month’s benefit for the first month of a new certification period, the household must fully complete the SNAP recertification process.

The SNAP recertification process is complete when prior to the expiration of the current certification period, the individual has:

• Completed an application for recertification;

• Participated in an interview, if required; and

• Provided all required verifications.

All requirements listed above must be met for the recertification process to be complete and SNAP benefits to continue uninterrupted. SNAP benefits are not closed or denied for households that are unable to obtain verifications and have contacted the Department on or before the last day of the month of the current certification period.

The department will require a face-to-face (in-person or phone) interview with individuals who were eligible online or by mail-in recertification method, but only provided their name, address, and signature, and failed to fully complete the recertification application.

For ESAP households, a face-to-face (in-person or phone) interview is required if verifications provided at redetermination are questionable or incomplete.

If the case is not processed within one month of the appointment date, the Department will contact the individual to verify that no information has changed since the individual’s recertification appointment.

If the individual has not participated in a recertification interview or provided required verification(s) by the end of the certification period, the recertification is denied by the last day of the month is which the certification period ends, See Section 161.07 , Termination at Recertification .

Benefits are prorated for the first month of the new certification period if the household completes the recertification process after the current certification period expires.

Exception: Benefits cannot be prorated if:

· the household provides all verifications requested within ten days of the request, even if they are received after the current certification period has expired, or

· there was a delay or agency error in processing due to the department.

Example: The household’s recertification period expires in September. On September 25th, the household submitted a recertification application but failed to submit all of the required verifications. The department requested missing verifications on September 25 th . The case auto closed on September 30; the last day of the certification period. On October 4, the household provided all required verifications to complete the recertification process. Benefits for October are reopened without proration.

IMPORTANT: Expedited SNAP benefits should not build within the first 30 days following a recertification period when the household provided their recertification application before the end of the current certification period but failed to provide the required verifications.

Example: The household’s recertification period expires in September. On September 15th, the household submitted a recertification application but failed to submit all of the required verifications. The Department requested missing verifications on September 20. The case auto closed on September 30; the last day of the certification period. On October 8, the household provided all required verifications to complete the recertification process. The case is not eligible for Expedited SNAP, benefits for October are prorated from October 8.

References : He-W 766.01; He-W 766.02; RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.14(b), (e) & (f)

161.07 Termination at Recertification (FSM)

SR 23-18 Dated 4/23 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

SNAP benefits terminate automatically at the end of the current certification period if the individual has not:

• completed an application;

• participated in an interview, if required; and

• provided all required verification prior to the expiration of the current certification period.

Deny the application within 30 days of receiving it if the individual has submitted a completed application and fails to:

• attend the interview appointment; or

• provide all required verification prior to the expiration of the current certification period.

See Part 127 , Interviews .

Deny the application for recertification when the individual fails or refuses to appear for a recertification interview without good cause and:

• fails to contact the Department for a second appointment; or

• requests another appointment but fails to appear for the rescheduled appointment.

Close or deny households that fail or refuse to cooperate in providing verification and do not contact the Department for assistance.

References : He-W 766.01; He-W 766.02; RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.2(e); 7 CFR 273.14(b)

body:
161.09 Untimely Reapplication (FSM)

SR 03-43 Dated 09/03 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Provide prorated benefits to households that file an application after any break in participation. A break in participation occurs when a client reapplies for benefits after the current certification has ended.

Example

A household ’ s benefits terminate in September. The household reapplies on October 6th. Prorate October ’ s Food Stamp benefits.

Exceptions:

• If the individual proves good cause for not filing a timely reapplication, or the time period for providing verification extends beyond the end of the certification period, process it as a timely recertification and restore any lost benefits.

• Do not prorate benefits for migrant and seasonal farm worker households unless the break in participation has been longer than 1 month.

*

Example

The household ’ s recertification expires in May. The household completes an application, and has an interview on May 17. Verification is provided to the Department on May 28th. Full benefits are issued for June, since the household has completed the reapplication process before the end of the current certification period. If the household had provided their verification anytime after June 1, there would have been a break in participation, and the household ’ s first month ’ s benefits would have been prorated.

Applications completed after the current certification period expires are treated the same as initial applications for benefit issuance purposes.

Exception: If the individual reapplies within 30 days after the current certification period expires, the individual does not need to reverify previously verified medical expenses or actual utility expenses if the source has not changed and the amount has changed by $25 or less per month.

References : He-W 766.01, He-W 766.02, R SA 161:4-a,IV , 7 CFR 273.10(a), 7 CFR 273.14(e)(3)

161 RECERTIFICATION (FSM)

SR 25-22 Dated 07/25 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

SNAP eligibility is determined for a specific period of time called the certification period. At the end of the certification period, entitlement to SNAP benefits ends. The individual must apply and be recertified in order to continue to receive SNAP benefits.

Eligibility for all individuals shall be recertified at regularly scheduled interval periods of either 6 or 36 months. See section 133.09 , Certification Periods.

References: He-W 746.02; He-W 766.01; He-W 766.02; RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.10(a)(2), (f), & (g)(2); 7 CFR 273.14

211.01 Who Must Be Members (FSM)

SR 24-22 Dated 09/24 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Certify the following as separate SNAP households:

· An individual who lives alone.

· A group of individuals who live, purchase food, and prepare meals together.

· An individual or group of individuals who live with others and who:

– usually purchases and prepares food separately from the others; or

– intends to purchase and prepare food separately from the others after certification.

· An individual age 60 or over (and spouse) who resides with others but cannot purchase and prepare food separately because of a permanent physical or mental disability, or a disability considered permanent under the Social Security Act. Allow separate household status only when all of the following apply:

– the gross income of the other household members (without the elderly person and spouse) is less than 165% of the federal poverty level;

– the elderly individual verifies the others’ income; and

– the elderly individual verifies the disability, if questionable.

· Siblings living together who purchase food and prepare meals separately and are not under the parental control of an adult household member.

· An individual or group of individuals who are blind or disabled residents of an authorized group living arrangement that meets the criteria in FSM 235.01 , Definition of Group Living Arrangement.

· A resident of federally subsidized housing for the elderly.

· A person with a substance or alcohol use disorder living and participating in a treatment program if the treatment center meets the criteria found in FSM 233 , ALCOHOL OR DRUG TREATMENT CENTERS.

Exception : Consider children living with their parents who participate in such treatment programs as members of the same household.

· A resident or family in a public or private nonprofit facility that provides shelter for the homeless or serves battered women and children.

Certify the following individuals as one household if they live together:

· Parents and children (natural, adoptive, or step) of any age.

Exceptions :

– Parents and their children age 22 or older may choose to be certified as separate households if they purchase and prepare food separately (or would if the parent were not age 60 or older and disabled).

– Certify an adopted child age 18 up to age 22 who no longer lives with his or her adoptive parents and now lives with his or her birth parent as a separate SNAP household from his or her birth parent when:

o the child provides a signed statement, under penalty of unsworn falsification, that he or she purchases food and prepares meals separately from his or her birth parent; and

o the birth parent has not reestablished parental rights over the adopted child.

· Children under 18 years of age who are under the parental control of an adult member of the household who is not their parent, even if the adult could qualify for separate household status because of age, target population criteria, or disability.

Spouses of household members. Spouses are either of 2 individuals who are defined as married under state law.

Note: A SNAP household can consist of individuals with multiple relationships that require the individuals to be considered one SNAP household. For example, a household consisting of a child under 18 years of age, the child’s parent, the child’s guardian, and the spouse of the guardian must be considered one SNAP household because:

· The child must be included with their parent;

· The child must be included with their guardian because a guardian is an adult who has parental control over the child; and

· The spouse must be included with the guardian.

References : He-W 756.03; He-W 756.05; RSA 161:4-a,IV; RSA 457:3; RSA 641:3; 7 CFR 273.1

211.03 Disqualified Individuals (FSM)

SR 23-28 Dated 08/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Certain individuals are disqualified for not complying with a program requirement.

Disqualify SNAP individuals for:

• Voluntary Quit. See PART 315 , VOLUNTARY QUIT, for more information.

• Failure to comply with SNAP work requirements. See PART 827 , DISQUALIFICATION PENALTIES , for more information.

• Being a fleeing felon, probation or parole violator, or an individual that has been convicted of certain crimes and is not in compliance with the terms of their sentence. See PART 319 , PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATORS, FLEEING FELONS, AND CERTAIN CONVICTED FELONS, for more information.

• Having fraudulently received multiple benefits. See PART 321 , INELIGIBILITY FOR FRAUDULENT RECEIPT OF MULTIPLE BENEFITS, for more information.

• Being adjudicated as an intentional program violator by a court of law, by an administrative disqualification hearing held by the Department, or by waiving their right to an administrative disqualification hearing. See PART 713 , INTENTIONAL PROGRAM VIOLATIONS (IPV), for more information.

Include the income and resources, but not the needs, of the disqualified individual when determining eligibility for assistance. See Section 611.05 , Income of Disqualified and Excluded Individuals , for more information .

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.1(b)(7); 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)-(ix); 7 CFR 273.11; 7 CFR 273.16

211.09 Who May Be Members (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Certify boarders, including foster care children, when both of the following apply:

• the household requests that the boarders be included, and

• the boarders pay the household a reasonable monthly cash payment for lodging and meals.

A reasonable monthly cash payment is determined as follows:

• boarders receiving more than 2 meals each day must pay an amount equal to or exceeding the maximum monthly coupon allotment for the size of the boarder household, or

• boarders receiving 1 or 2 meals each day must pay an amount equal to or exceeding 2/3 of the maximum monthly coupon allotment for the size of the boarder household.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.1(b)(3)

211.11 Who Is Not a Member (FSM)

SR 23-37 Dated 10/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Do not include the following in the SNAP household:

• Individuals disqualified for any of the reasons listed in FSM 211.03 , Disqualified Individuals ;

• Individuals excluded for any of the reasons listed in FSM 611.05 , Income of Disqualified and Excluded Individuals ;

• Non-household members who reside with the certified household. Non-household members are the following:

- roomers;

- live-in attendants;

- ineligible students; or

- others sharing living quarters but purchasing and preparing meals separately.

• Boarders, including foster care children who are not considered members of the certified household with whom they live.

• Residents of institutions who receive the majority of their meals (over 50% of three meals daily) from an institution not authorized to accept SNAP.

Exception : Residents of authorized group living arrangements, drug or alcohol treatment programs, shelters for the homeless or battered women and children, or federally subsidized housing for the elderly may be eligible.

• New household members still certified in another household.

• New households that have splintered off an existing household and the members are still open in the former household because the advance notice period has yet to expire. The new household will be eligible the month following the month in which the advance notice period expires.

Exception : Residents in shelters for battered women and children may receive up to 2 allotments in 1 month. See FSM 237.05 , Two Issuances in the Same Month .

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 273.1; 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)-(ix); 7 CFR 273.11(g)(2); 7 CFR 273.16

body:
211.13 Shared Child Custody Situations

SR 13-27 Dated 09/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

When two households share custody of a child, and both households request Food Stamp benefits for that child, include the child in the Food Stamp household that first requests Food Stamp benefits for the child.

The household considered to be the “household that first requests Food Stamp benefits for the child” is the first household in which the child is included as a Food Stamp applicant or recipient. Throughout the explanation of this policy, this household will be known as the “current household.” The household which requests Food Stamp benefits for the child after the child has already been included as a member of the current household will be known as the “second household.”

The child remains in the current household, unless all of the following occur:

• the child ’ s circumstances change and the child now primarily resides in the second household;

• the second household requests Food Stamp benefits for the child; and

• the second household provides verification that the child primarily resides in the second household.

Remove the child from the current household and place the child in the second household when the second household provides a statement:

• indicating the child resides in the second household; and

• that is signed by:

- the casehead of the current household; or

- the child, if that child is at least age 18.

The child must be removed from the current household and placed in the second household within 30 days of the date the District Office receives the statement described above. However, it is best practice to remove the child from the current household and place the child in the second household within 10 days of the date the District Office receives the statement. Processing these cases within a 10-day timeframe will ensure the child does not receive an additional allotment of Food Stamps benefits in the current household after the 30th day has passed due to the passing of any benefit pull down dates.

NOTE: The following policy should only be applied when the second household indicates:

• the current household will not sign a statement regardless of whether the child primarily resides in the second household; or

• the second household is uncertain as to whose household the child is currently included.

When the second household indicates a statement signed by the current household cannot be obtained, the second household may provide sufficient evidence that the child primarily resides in the second household. Sufficient evidence can be any verification that reasonably proves the child resides in the second household the majority of the time, including but not limited to:

• current day care records;

• current school records;

• current medical records; and

• court orders.

NOTE: Court orders should not be the sole basis for this determination. Many times court orders are not followed after they are established. If a court order is provided, the second household must provide verification in addition to the court order to prove the child resides in the second household the majority of the time.

The District Office Supervisor, or an individual designated by the District Office Supervisor, reviews the verification described above to determine if the documents provided do, in fact, reasonably prove the child resides in the second household the majority of the time.

When the verification provided by the second household is determined to reasonably prove that the child resides in the second household the majority of the time, the District Office must:

• following confidentiality guidelines, notify the current household that a second household is claiming that a child who is included in the current household resides in the second household the majority of the time and that if the current household does not take any action, the child will be removed from their household and their Food Stamp benefits may decrease; and

• provide the current household 10 days to send in verification that reasonably proves that the child resides in the current household the majority of the time.

Remove the child from the current household and place the child in the second household when the current household:

• does not provide verification within 10 days of notification; or

• provides verification that does not reasonably prove the child resides in the current household the majority of the time.

The child must be removed from the current household and placed in the second household within 30 days of the date the District Office Supervisor, or an individual designated by the District Office Supervisor, determines the documents provided do, in fact, reasonably prove the child resides in the second household the majority of the time. However, it is best practice to remove the child from the current household and place the child in the second household within 10 days of the date the determination is made. Processing these cases within a 10-day timeframe will ensure the child does not receive an additional allotment of Food Stamps benefits in the current household after the 30th day has passed due to the passing of any benefit pull down dates.

The child remains in the current household when:

• the verification provided by the second household is determined to not reasonably prove that the child resides in the second household the majority of the time;

• the second household fails to provide verification within 10 days of the request; or

• both Food Stamp households provide verification that reasonably proves the child resides in their Food Stamp household the majority of the time.

Special Circumstances for 50/50 Splits Only

The following policy should only be applied in the most extreme circumstances when:

• a court order indicates there is a 50/50 custody split between the two households; and

• the District Office Supervisor, or an individual designated by the District Office Supervisor, has applied the Shared Custody policy above and determined there is an exact 50/50 custody split between the two households.

When two households have an exact 50/50 custody split, include the child in the household who provided more meals to the child over the past six months. Due to the variations in the number of days in a month, six months is standardized at a 26-week period when applying this policy.

Give credit to each household for providing meals when that household has custody of the child during the majority of the mealtime hours, as defined below:

• Breakfast time hours are the hours between 12:00 am and 10:00 am;

• Lunch time hours are the hours between 10:01 am and 3:00 pm; and

• Dinner time hours are the hours between 3:01 pm and 11:59 pm.

Use the parenting plan in the court order to determine which household has custody of the child during mealtime hours. The parenting plan indicates when each household has custody of the child. The hours each parent has custody of the child is compared to the hours laid out above. The parent who has custody of the child for the majority of the mealtime receives credit for that meal. The parent who receives credit for more meals over a 26-week period is considered to have provided more meals to the child over the past 6 months. It is the responsibility of the second household to provide the parenting plan within 10 days of the request .

When the parenting plan indicates which household drops the child off at school, the household who drops the child off at school receives credit for the mealtime hours the child spends at school.

Remove the child from the current household and place the child in the second household when the District Office determines that the parenting plan indicates the second household provided more meals to the child over the past six months.

The child must be removed from the current household and placed in the second household within 30 days of the date the District Office determines that the parenting plan indicates the second household provided more meals to the child over the past six months. However, it is best practice to remove the child from the current household and place the child in the second household within 10 days of the date the determination is made. Processing these cases within a 10-day timeframe will ensure the child does not receive an additional allotment of Food Stamps benefits in the current household after the 30th day has passed due to the passing of any benefit pull down dates.

The child remains in the current household when:

• the second household fails to provide the parenting plan within 10 days of the request;

• the District Office determines that the parenting plan indicates the current household provided more meals to the child over the past six months; or

• the District Office determines that the parenting plan indicates both households provide the same number of meals to the child over the past six months.

References : He-W 756.01, RSA 161:4-a,IV, RSA 167:3-c,I, 7 CFR 273.1(c); 7 CFR 273.3(a)

213 REQUIRED VERIFICATION (FSM)

SR 14-15 Dated 12/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

The individual must provide verification of factors affecting household composition if questionable.

Assist the individual in obtaining verification if the individual is incapable of providing it because of a mental or physical disability.

Questionable Factor Acceptable Verification Household size • A signed statement by an individual residing outside of the household who knows the individuals in the household. - The statement must include a listing of the individuals in the household and their address. Marital Status • Original or certified copies of legal documents such as marriage licenses or divorce decrees. • Signed statements from relatives or individuals residing in the community. • Other similar verification. Purchasing and preparing food separately • A statement signed by all adults residing within the household. • A signed statement by an individual residing outside of the household who knows the individuals in the household. • A completed BFA Form 768, Shared Shelter Arrangements . • Other similar verification. In a situation in which it is an adopted child > 18 and < 22 who is now living with his or her birthparents, a signed statement, under penalty of unsworn falsification, that he or she purchases food and prepares meals separately from his or her birthparent. Disability If not apparent, a physician’s statement that the disability prevents the individual from purchasing and preparing food. Income less than 165% of net monthly limit See Chapter 500 , Income .

References : He-W 701.03; He-W 742.02; He-W 756.05; RSA 161:4-a,IV; RSA 641:3; 7 CFR 273.1; 7 CFR 273.2

Introduction (FSM)

SR 98-10 Dated 04/98 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________________

The New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Family Assistance (DFA), administers public assistance programs in accordance with state law and federal laws and regulations. This manual contains the official DFA policy governing the Food Stamp Program.

DFA administers other programs providing

• financial and medical assistance for the elderly, blind, and disabled, and

• financial and medical assistance and employment and training support services for families with dependent children, and child care reimbursement assistance for families requiring child care due to participation in employment, training, or educational activities.

Policy governing these programs is contained in the Adult Assistance Manual and in the Family Assistance Manual, respectively. Information on the purpose and instructions for completion of forms referred to in this manual are contained in the DFA Forms Manual.

How This Manual Is Updated (FSM)

SR 98-10 Dated 04/98 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________________

Policy revisions are issued by Supervisory Releases (SR), which contain a narrative describing the changes. Replacement manual pages are issued with the SR to holders of the paper version of the manual. The electronic version of the manual is centrally updated through the Version Control process.

The header of each page identifies:

• the Chapter, Part, or Section number and name,

• the manual affected (AAM),

• the SR number which released the policy,

• the effective date of the policy, and

• for those with access to the Department ’ s computer network, an automated link to Previous Policy, if applicable.

Part numbers are three digits; the first digit identifies the chapter (e.g., part 409 is from chapter 400). Section numbers further divide the parts and use the part number followed by a decimal point and two digits (e.g., 409.01 refers to chapter 400, part 409, section 01).

As this manual is the basis for administering and implementing DFA programs, it will be updated as policy is revised.

227.01 Individuals Not Considered Strikers (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

An individual is not considered a striker if the individual is:

• exempt from work registration for any reason other than employment (such as care of a child) the day before the strike;

• not participating in the strike, but cannot work because of the strike (such as flight attendants who cannot work because of an airline pilot strike or truck drivers who cannot do their jobs because the strike has left them with nothing to deliver);

• not part of the bargaining unit and does not want to cross the picket line because of fear of personal injury or death; or

• locked out of the job by the employer, including individuals who were considered strikers before the lockout.

References : He-W 746.02(e), RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.1(e), 7 USC 2015(d)(3)

227.03 Striker Eligibility (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

A household with a striking member is not eligible for Food Stamp benefits unless the household was eligible for benefits, or would have been eligible for benefits, the day before the strike and is otherwise eligible at the time of application.

All eligibility factors must have been met as of the day before the strike for the household ’ s current eligibility to be considered.

References : He-W 746.02(e), RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.1(e), 7 USC 2015(d)(3)

body:
227.05 Treatment of Striker Income (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Use the income of all household members (including the striker) as of the day before the strike, and assuming the strike did not occur. If the household is ineligible, deny the household.

If the household would have been eligible before the strike, compute current eligibility as follows:

1. Compare the striker ’ s income on the day before the strike with the striker ’ s current income (including union benefits and part-time jobs). Count the higher of the two incomes.

2. Add the striker ’ s higher income to the current income of other household members.

If the household is not currently eligible, deny or terminate the household.

If the household is eligible based on current income and income before the strike, determine whether the household meets all other eligibility criteria both currently and before the strike. If the household is still eligible, higher income figure must also be used to determine the household’s benefits.

References : He-W 746.02(e), RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.1(e), 7 USC 2015(d)(3)

____________________________________________________________

The individual must provide verification of the following circumstances when questionable:

• employees have been locked out;

• employees are prevented from working due to other striking employees; or

• crossing the picket line is a threat to physical safety.

227 STRIKERS (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

A striker is anyone involved in a strike or concerted work stoppage by employees (including a stoppage due to the expiration of a collective bargaining agreement), and any concerted slowdown or other concerted interruption of operations by employees.

Striker status ends only when the individual returns to the job, retires, quits, is locked out, or is fired, regardless of the length of the strike.

Exception: Striking federal, state, or local government employees who are dismissed because of participating in the strike are considered to have voluntarily quit without good cause.

References : He-W 746.02(e), RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 273.1(e), 7 CFR 273.7(j)(3)(ii), 7 USC 2015(d)(1)(D)(iv) & (d)(3), 29 USC 142(2)

229.03 Definition of Disabled (FSM)

SR 23-26 Dated 06/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Disabled means any of the following:

● Individuals receiving ANB or APTD financial or medical assistance; ● Disabled individuals approved for SSI or Social Security disability or blindness payments; ● Veterans who: § receive U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) benefits because of a total (100%) service-connected or non-service-connected disability; § according to the VA, need regular aid and attendance; or § are permanently housebound; ● Surviving spouses of deceased veterans who the VA has determined need regular aid and attendance, are permanently housebound or could be considered permanently disabled by Social Security criteria, and are approved for VA benefits because of the veteran's death; ● Surviving children (of any age) of deceased veterans who the VA has determined are permanently incapable of self-support or could be considered permanently disabled by Social Security criteria, and are approved for VA benefits because of the veteran's death; ● Individuals receiving disability retirement benefits from any government agency for a disability that could be considered permanent by Social Security criteria; or ● Individuals receiving Railroad Retirement Disability who are also covered by Medicare or receiving Railroad Retirement Disability and considered permanently disabled by Social Security criteria.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; 7 CFR 271.2; 7 USC 2012(j)

229.05 Social Security's Permanent Disability Criteria (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Social Security presumes permanent disability status for any of the following:

• permanent loss of use of both hands, both feet, or one hand and one foot,

• amputation of a leg at the hip,

• amputation of a leg or foot because of diabetes mellitus or peripheral vascular diseases,

• total deafness, not correctable by surgery or hearing aid,

• statutory blindness, unless caused by cataracts or detached retina,

• IQ of 59 or less, established after the individual reaches age 16.

• spinal cord or nerve root lesions resulting in paraplegia or quadriplegia,

• multiple sclerosis in which there is damage to the nervous system because of scattered areas of inflammation. The inflammation recurs and has progressed to varied interference with the function of the nervous system, including severe muscle weakness, paralysis, and vision and speech defects,

• muscular dystrophy with irreversible wasting of the muscles, impairing the use of arms or legs,

• Down ’ s Syndrome (mongolism),

• Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS),

• impaired kidney function caused by chronic renal disease, resulting in severely reduced function which may require dialysis or kidney transplant, or

• amputation of a limb of an individual age 55 or older.

Social Security considers certain additional conditions as permanent disabilities. Social Security refers to these conditions as "MINE" (Medical Improvement Not Expected) disabilities. Each DHHS District Office Supervisor has a copy of the MINE list.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 271.2, 7 USC 2012(j), 20 CFR 416, subpart I

229.07 Required Verification (FSM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

The individual must provide verification of factors affecting target population status if questionable. Assist the individual in obtaining required verification if the individual is incapable of providing it.

If the individual is claiming a disability which is not apparent, request a signed statement from a physician or licensed or certified psychologist which substantiates the individual ’ s claim.

If the individual is claiming a permanent disability based on approval for disability benefits, request a statement from the agency approving the benefits if questionable.

If needed, obtain verification of Railroad Retirement disability benefits and Medicare eligibility from the Railroad Retirement Board, P.O. Box 2448, Boston, MA 02208, or telephone (617) 424-5790.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 271.2, 7 CFR 273.2(f)(1)(viii), 7 USC 2012(j)

229 TARGET POPULATION (FSM)

SR 99-25 Dated 06/99 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Certain elderly or disabled individuals are defined as the target population. Allow target population individuals the following additional income deductions and options:

*

• Gross income test — exempt a household with 1 or more target population individuals from the gross income test.

• Medical expense deduction — allow a medical expense deduction for a household with a target population individual who has medical bills that exceed $35 a month.

• Excess shelter expense deduction — allow a household with a target population individual an excess shelter deduction for the full monthly amount that exceeds 50% of the household ’ s monthly income after other deductions.

References : He-W 758.01, RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 271.2, 7 CFR 273.9(a), (d)(3), & (d)(6)(ii), 7 USC 2012(j), 7 USC 2020(e)(2)(A)

231.05 Expanded Categorical Eligibility Criteria (FSM)

SR 22-37 Dated 01/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Households may be considered Expanded Categorically eligible for SNAP if the household is not already categorically eligible due to receipt of public assistance (PA) or SSI, when:

· the household’s gross income is less than or equal to 200% of the federal poverty income guidelines; and

· the household would receive or be eligible to receive non-cash or in-kind services from a program that is less than 50% funded with State or Federal money counted for Maintenance of Effort (MOE) purposes under Title IV-A.

The Department developed BFA Form 77u, Community Resources , to meet the last requirement.

Households meeting expanded categorical eligibility criteria are not subject to the SNAP resource test.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; RSA 167:4,I(a); 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2) & (j)(4); 7 CFR 273.9(a)

231.01 Categorical Eligibility Criteria (FSM)

SR 22-37 Dated 01/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Households that purchase and prepare food together are categorically eligible for SNAP if all members receive public assistance (PA) or SSI. PA means FANF, OAA, APTD, or ANB financial assistance.

Exception: IV-E foster care and Refugee Cash Assistance are not considered PA for purposes of this category of categorical eligibility.

Categorical eligibility via receipt of PA or SSI includes households that:

· Have been determined eligible for PA or SSI but whose financial benefits have not yet begun; · Receive zero PA financial benefits because their PA grant amount is less than $10; · Receive zero PA or SSI benefits because their payments have been suspended or are being recouped; or · Have an ineligible alien or student member who does not get PA or SSI.

Households meeting categorical eligibility criteria are not subject to the SNAP resource test or additional income tests.

References : RSA 167:4,I(a); RSA 167:7,IV; 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2) & (j)(4); 7 CFR 273.9(a)

231.03 Required Verification for Categorical Eligibility (FSM)

SR 22-37 Dated 01/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Consider categorically eligible households to have already verified the following eligibility factors:

• resources;

• social security enumeration requirements;

• sponsored alien information; and

• residency.

If questionable, require verification of each of the following:

• the household is composed solely of individuals receiving public assistance or SSI;

• the household meets the SNAP household composition criteria; and

• the household does not include someone disqualified due to an intentional program violation or noncompliance with work registration requirements.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV; RSA 167:4,I(a); 7 CFR 273.2(f), (j)(2) & (j)(4); 7 CFR 273.9(a)

233 RESIDENTS OF DRUG OR ALCOHOL TREATMENT CENTERS (FSM)

SR 25-11 Dated 05/25 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Individuals who regularly participate as residents in a drug or alcohol treatment program may participate in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) only if the treatment center meets one of the following criteria:

• is authorized by the USDA to accept SNAP benefits;

• is a publicly operated community mental health center under Part B of Title XIX of the Public Health Service Act; or

• is nonprofit and has a contract with, or is authorized by, the State of New Hampshire to provide treatment that can lead to the rehabilitation of drug addicts or alcoholics.

An employee designated by the treatment center must act as the authorized representative (AR) to apply on behalf of the individual.

References : RSA 161:4-a,IV, 7 CFR 271.2, 7 CFR 273.2(n)(1)(ii), 7 CFR 273.11(e), 7 CFR 274.7(g)(3)(i), 7 CFR 278.1(e), 7 CFR 278.2(g), 7 USC 2012(h), (k)(5), & (m)(5)(E)
